answer.label: Not Hemingway’s exact words — a euphemistic paraphrase
answer.sourceLine: No source records Hemingway saying “garbage.” The closest attested version — “The first draft of anything is shit” — comes from a memoir published 23 years after his death, recalling a 1934 conversation from memory.

source.excerpt: The first draft of anything is shit.
trail: The earliest documented appearance is Arnold Samuelson’s memoir With Hemingway: A Year in Key West and Cuba ↗, published in 1984, recording a remark Hemingway made to him in 1934.
Samuelson’s manuscript was not published in his lifetime — it surfaced only after his death and reached print via Esquire in 1985 and the book in 1984, per Quote Investigator’s timeline ↗.
Quote Investigator’s full citation trail documents only two variants, “shit” and “rubbish” — never “garbage,” per its sourced investigation ↗.
The “garbage” wording circulates uncited on quote-aggregator pages such as Quotes Street ↗, which gives no source at all.
source.excerptNote: As recorded by Arnold Samuelson, quoting Hemingway’s advice to him in Key West, 1934. The word “garbage” does not appear in this or any other documented source.

source.rightsNote: The exact phrase “garbage” has no identifiable origin to attach rights to. Even the attested “shit” wording sits inside Arnold Samuelson’s in-copyright 1984 memoir (his estate/Random House), not in any Hemingway-authored text, so no public-domain claim can honestly be made here.

author.heading: Who was Ernest Hemingway?
author.bio: Ernest Hemingway was an American writer celebrated for a spare, understated prose style that reshaped 20th-century fiction. His novels include The Sun Also Rises, A Farewell to Arms, and The Old Man and the Sea, and he received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1954.

misattribution.heading: Often misattributed
misattribution.intro: This is less a case of the quote belonging to someone else, and more a case of a real (if shaky) quote being re-worded until the paper trail disappears.

items.why: Sites like Quotes Street ↗ print “garbage” with no citation at all — a family-friendly swap for “shit” that has taken on a life of its own.
Even the “shit” version traces to one source: Samuelson’s memoir, written from memory and not published until 1984–85, decades after the 1934 exchange it describes, as Quote Investigator lays out ↗.

misattribution.truthLine: Hemingway likely did say something like this to Samuelson in 1934 about rewriting A Farewell to Arms — but the words on quote sites today, “garbage” included, are several steps removed from anything he is actually documented to have said. See Quote Investigator’s full history ↗.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The line usually quoted as “The first draft of anything is garbage” is a softened, internet-era paraphrase. No book, letter, or interview ever printed those words from Hemingway.

The closest real source is Arnold Samuelson’s 1984 memoir With Hemingway: A Year in Key West and Cuba, which recalls Hemingway telling him in 1934: “The first draft of anything is shit.” Samuelson was a 22-year-old aspiring writer who spent about a year as Hemingway’s deckhand and pupil in Key West; his manuscript went unpublished until after his own death, so the exact wording rests on one man’s decades-old memory, not on anything Hemingway wrote himself.
context.pull: No citation anywhere uses the word “garbage.”
